conventions: **Styles come from frontail.** Import `@marthvon/frontail/components/index.css` once, or import only the stylesheets each component lists under **Stylesheet**, including the ones it depends on. Without them the components render unstyled.

**Import frontail's utilities too.** Many components rely on its utility stylesheets (`utilities/layouts.css`, `modal.css`, `3d.css`, `animate.css`, `layers.css`, plus `theme/keyframes.css`). Import them all once next to the component stylesheets.

**Class props are for containers only.** `className` styles the root and `xxxClass` props style named inner boxes. Text pieces are never styled by a class prop; replace them with a render prop / snippet instead.

**`Content` props take a string or a render function.** Props typed `Content` (or `Content<[args]>`) accept a plain string, which keeps the default element and only changes its text, or a function / snippet, which replaces the element entirely and receives the listed arguments.

**State is controlled by you.** Components report changes through callbacks and render what you pass back. Select, FilterRow, SortHeading and ResourceTable keep no copy of `value`, `values`, `query`, `sorts`, `page` or `selected`; update your state in the callback or nothing changes.
**Ids.** `formId` prefixes generated ids so labels and error messages stay linked; every instance still gets a unique id, so repeating the same `label` is safe.

**Presets are const enums.** `DropdownPreset`, `PanelPreset`, `CardPreset` and `Interact` come from the `presets.client` module. Each preset is a set of class names, so pass the enum member, never a string you typed yourself.
**Layering.** Popovers use `--z-popover` (50), their click-out backdrops `--z-backdrop` (40) and sticky headers `--z-sticky` (2). The `Z` export from `utils` holds the same scale.

**`zIndex` for layers opened from other layers.** Dropdown, Select, DatePickerInput, PhoneField, Tooltip, ResourceTable and TextEditor take `zIndex`, which sets the popups and backdrop of that component (and of everything rendered inside it) to that value. When a component opens from inside a dialog or another popup, pass the opener's z-index plus one, e.g. `zIndex={Z.modal + 1}` inside a dialog at `Z.modal`, and keep counting up for each deeper level, so the newest layer is always on top. Never put a dropdown inside a parent with `transform`, `filter`, `opacity` below 1 or its own `z-index`, because that parent traps the popover underneath later content.
**Optional peers.** TextEditor needs `@codemirror/commands`, `@codemirror/state`, `@codemirror/view` and `markdown-it`; QrCode needs `qrcode-generator`. Install them only if you use those components.
Callbacks are camelCase (`onChange`, `onToggle`, `onSelect`). Render props are functions returning `ReactNode`, for example `option={(option) => {option.label}}`.
Where the Svelte package uses a named slot, React takes a prop of the same name: CardA and CardB `image`, Panel `modal`.

Components are client components (`"use client"`). In server-rendered or static pages import presets from `presets.server`; on client-only pages `presets.client` lets the compiler inline the class names.
Components that list **Ref** forward a ref to that element, so `ref` works like it does on the native element.

choosing.use: TextboxB (outlined, label floats onto the border) for most forms; TextboxC (outlined, label always on the border, allows a placeholder); TextboxA (filled, label below the box). All three become a textarea when `height` is above 3.25 (rem). TextboxB and C reserve a line for the error so the form never jumps.

choosing.need: A password, phone number or code
choosing.use: PasswordField (`variant` a/b/c picks the textbox; or set `secret` on any Textbox), PhoneField (country dial code + number, stores digits only; pass a Textbox as `field` to match your form), Digitbox (one box per character, for OTP codes).
TextEditor: a markdown editor with a toolbar and insertable `{{variables}}`.
Select for a form value (single or `multiple`). Dropdown only for a free-form menu of your own markup (actions, account menu); it has no value.
DatePickerInput for a form field that opens a calendar; DatePicker for an always-visible calendar.
Slider for one value, DualSlider for a min/max pair. Both snap to `step` and keep their labels a fixed width.
FieldGuide: clips long text to `limit` and shows See more / See less only when it overflows.
ResourceTable (sorting, paging, selection, row actions, stacks into cards on narrow screens). Put a FilterRow above it for search and filters, and render SortHeading in its `sortHeading` slot.
UploadPanel: drop zone, queue with progress, retry. You supply the actual `upload(file, progress)` function.
FileViewer: images, video, PDF, HTML, plain text, or a fallback card.
ImageCarousel (3D carousel with autoplay), GridView (masonry of your own tiles), SmartGridView (masonry that places tiles by aspect ratio and supports infinite scroll).
CardA flips to its back on hover/click; CardB slides a gradient panel over an image.
Panel: a side or bottom sheet the user drags to resize, optionally snapping to set sizes.

choosing.need: A hint on hover or focus
choosing.use: Tooltip: wraps a trigger and shows `content` (a string or snippet) beside it on hover and keyboard focus. Use Dropdown instead when the popup must open on click.
Breadcrumbs for a page trail; QrCode to render a scannable code as SVG.

recipes.title: Searchable, sortable, paged table
A filter control inside FilterRow
recipes.code:
<FilterRow id="people" query={query} onInput={setQuery} sizes={[FILTER_SIZE]} applied={!!role}
  controls={(slot) => <Select label="Role" className="filter-slot" style={slot(0)} options={roles} value={role} clearable onChange={setRole} />} />

components.name: Breadcrumbs
components.summary: A trail of links to the current page. The last crumb is the current page and is not a link.
components.example: <Breadcrumbs separator="/" crumbs={[{ label: "Home", href: "/", home: true }, { label: "Clients", href: "/clients" }, { label: "Ada Lovelace" }]} />
notes: `crumbs` is `{ label, href?, home? }[]`; `home: true` shows `homeIcon` before that crumb.
`separator` and `homeIcon` accept text ("/", "⌂") or your own element.

components.name: CardA
components.summary: A card that flips from an image to a back face on hover, click, or both.
components.example:
}>
Back of the card
notes: Give the parent a fixed height; the card fills it.
`interact` takes `Interact.HOVER`, `Interact.CLICK` or `Interact.HOVER_N_CLICK`.

components.name: CardB
components.summary: An image card that slides a gradient panel with your content over it on hover.
components.example:

Revealed on hover
notes: `from_color` is the Tailwind gradient start, e.g. `from-indigo-900`.
`preset` is a `CardPreset` member: TO_RIGHT, TO_LEFT, TO_TOP, TO_BOTTOM, or the `_AT_HALF` versions that stop half way.

components.name: DatePicker
components.summary: An always-visible month calendar. Values are ISO dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
components.example: <DatePicker label="Due date" formId="task" value={due} onChange={setDue} />
notes: `locale` sets month and weekday names, e.g. `fr-FR`.
Below 240px wide it switches to compact day labels; `dayMini` customises those.
`day`, `weekday` and `heading` receive `DayCtx`, `WeekdayCtx` and `HeadingCtx` and replace those cells.
`onChange` fires when a day is picked.

components.name: DatePickerInput
components.summary: A text box that opens a DatePicker in a dropdown. Typing a valid `YYYY-MM-DD` also works; an impossible date reverts on blur.
components.css: `datepicker.css`, `dropdown.css`, the stylesheet of the text box (`textbox.a.css` by default) and frontail utilities `modal.css` and `layouts.css`
components.example:
<DatePickerInput label="Start date" formId="booking" value={start} onChange={setStart} />
<DatePickerInput label="Due date" formId="task" value={due} onChange={setDue} field={(input) => <TextboxB {...input} />} />
notes: The text box is TextboxA by default. Pass `field` to use any Textbox instead: spread the props it receives (`formId`, `label`, `value`, `maxLength`, `guard` and the input/blur handlers) onto it, exactly like PhoneField's `field`.
`preset={DropdownPreset.TOP}` opens the calendar above the box.
Values are ISO dates; `onChange` fires when a day is picked or a valid date is typed.

components.name: Digitbox
components.summary: One box per character for verification codes. Focus moves to the next box as the user types.
components.example: <form><Digitbox label="Code" formId="verify" name="code" digits={6} onChange={() => submit()} /></form>
notes: With `name`, the combined value is submitted once under that name through a hidden input.
`isNumeric={false}` allows letters.
Boxes shrink to fit a narrow container.

components.name: Dropdown
components.summary: A trigger that opens your own menu markup. It holds no value; use Select for form values.
components.example: )}> Account
notes: `preset` picks the direction (DropdownPreset.BOTTOM, TOP, LEFT, RIGHT); `interact` picks hover, click or both.
`clickOut` adds a backdrop that closes the menu on an outside click (click mode only).
Style the menu box with `innerModalClass`.
`menu` is an array of nodes; `children` is the trigger.

components.name: DualSlider
components.summary: A range slider with a minimum and a maximum thumb.
components.example: <DualSlider label="Price" formId="filters" min={0} max={500} step={10} labelPos="o" labelParse={(n) => `$${n}`} />
notes: Values snap to `min + n × step` (default step 1) and are rounded to the step's decimals.
`labelPos="o"` shows the values outside the bar in fixed-width labels; `"i"` shows them inside the thumbs.
`labelParse` formats the shown value, e.g. `(n) => `$${n}``.
The current value is `"min,max"` on the hidden input (the ref).
`onChange` receives that string when a drag ends.

components.name: FieldGuide
components.summary: Help text for a field. Text taller than `limit` is clipped with a fade and an animated See more / See less toggle; shorter text shows in full with no toggle.
components.example: <FieldGuide text="We send a confirmation link to this address. It expires after 24 hours." limit={2} expand="Read more" />
notes: `limit` is in rem (default 3, about three lines).
Overflow is measured by one shared ResizeObserver, so it is cheap to use many.

components.name: FileViewer
components.summary: Previews a file by type: image, video, PDF, HTML, text, or a fallback card for anything else.
notes: The kind is inferred from `type` (MIME) and `name`; pass `kind` to force it.
Pass `content` to show text you already have without fetching `src`.
`prev`/`next` with `onPrev`/`onNext` add arrows for browsing a list.
Give it a sized parent; it fills it.

components.name: FilterRow
components.summary: A search box plus filter controls that share one row and wrap behind a "More filters" toggle when space runs out.
components.css: `filter_row.css`, `field.css`, plus `select.css` for Selects in the row
components.example:
<FilterRow id="people" query={query} onInput={setQuery} sizes={[FILTER_SIZE]} applied={!!role} clearable={!!query || !!role}
  onClear={() => { setQuery(""); setRole(""); }}
  controls={(slot) => <Select label="Role" className="filter-slot" style={slot(0)} options={roles} value={role} clearable onChange={setRole} />} />
notes: `sizes` describes each control in `controls` (use the presets in the `filters` module); `controls(slot)` must give control `i` the class `filter-slot` and the style `slot(i)`. Without both the controls overlap the toggles.

The More filters toggle only appears when the controls wrap past one line; FilterRow knows the width at which that happens from `sizes`, so it costs no layout measurement. A custom `toggle` should keep the `filter-toggle` class to get this.
`applied` highlights the toggle; `clearable` + `onClear` shows a Clear button; `onRefresh` adds a refresh button and `refreshing` spins it.
`id` must be unique on the page.

components.name: GridView
components.summary: A masonry grid of your own tiles, kept in order across columns.
components.example: [photo.id, ]))} />
notes: Columns follow the container width (1 below 28rem, up to 7 when very wide); `columns` forces a count.
`childrens` is a record of key → node.
`onScrollEnd` fires when the user scrolls to the bottom, for infinite loading.

components.name: ImageCarousel
components.summary: A 3D carousel with arrows, optional autoplay, dot indicators and a progress loader.
components.css: `image_carousel.css`, plus `linear_loader.css` for `loader`, and frontail utilities `3d.css`, `layouts.css` and `modal.css`
components.example: [photo.id, ])} />
notes: Slides need an intrinsic width (an image, or a box like `w-96 max-w-full`); `w-full` slides collapse.
Side slides are pushed about 250px outward, so give it a full-width row, not a narrow column.
`timeout` (seconds) enables autoplay; `cursor_color` enables the arrows and colours them.
`loader` paints a bar that fills over `timeout` seconds and restarts on every slide change; `fill_color` colours the bar and `empty_color` the track. Clicking it pauses or resumes autoplay.

components.name: Panel
components.summary: A drawer over your content that the user drags to resize, from the top, bottom, left or right.
components.example:
Details

}>
Main content
notes: Put it in a positioned parent with a fixed height; it fills it.
`default_ratio` is a CSS size (`"40%"`) or the index of a lock point in `ratio`.
`ratio` alternates bounds, comparators and lock points: `[0, "<=", 0.25, "<", 0.5, "<=", 0.75, "<=", 1]` snaps to 25% below half and 75% above it; `"x"` as a lock point means stay where dropped.

components.name: PasswordField
components.summary: A password field: a thin wrapper that renders TextboxA, B or C (`variant`) with `secret` on, password autocomplete and a 64-character limit.
components.css: the chosen textbox's stylesheet (`textbox.a.css` or `textbox.b.css`) plus `textbox.reveal.css`
components.example: <PasswordField variant="b" label="Password" formId="signup" autoComplete="new-password" value={password} error={issue} onChange={setPassword} />
notes: Everything else is passed to the textbox, so its props (`error`, `formId`, `showIcon`, `hideIcon`, `revealed`, `boxClass`, …) work here too.
Use `autoComplete="new-password"` (Svelte: `autocomplete`) on sign-up and change-password forms.
For a show/hide toggle on any other field, set `secret` on the textbox directly.
`onChange` receives the new value as a string.

components.name: PhoneField
components.summary: A country dial-code picker with flags plus a number box. The value is digits only, dial code first (`61412345678`).
components.css: `phone_field.css`, `field.css`, `select.css`, `dropdown.css`, plus the stylesheet of any Textbox passed as `field`
components.example:
<PhoneField label="Phone" formId="contact" value={phone} error={phoneIssue(phone)} onChange={setPhone} />
<PhoneField label="Mobile" formId="contact" value={mobile} onChange={setMobile} field={(input) => <TextboxB {...input} />} />
notes: By default the number box is a plain rounded input with the label above and the error below.

Pass `field` to render the number box with any Textbox instead: spread the props it receives (`label`, `value`, `error`, `maxLength`, `mode`, autocomplete and the input/blur handlers) onto the textbox. The textbox then shows the label and error, and the country picker restyles itself to match TextboxA, B or C.
The country menu opens above by default; pass `preset={DropdownPreset.BOTTOM}` near the top of a page.
Validate with `phoneIssue(value)` from the `phone` module; `countries` limits or reorders the list.

components.name: QrCode
components.summary: Renders text or a URL as a scalable QR code SVG.
components.example: <QrCode value="https://example.com/invite/42" label="Invite link" className="w-40" />
notes: Needs the `qrcode-generator` peer dependency.
Size it with `className` (e.g. `w-40`).
`level` is error correction (L, M, Q, H); `quiet` is the margin in modules.

components.name: ResourceTable
components.summary: A data table with sorting, paging, selection, status pills and row actions. Below a container width it turns each row into a card.

props.name: rowEdge
props.type: ((row: Row) => { tone: string; label: string; } | null)

props.name: content
props.type: ((row: Row, key: string, text: string) => ReactNode)

props.name: range
props.type: ((from: number, to: number, total: number) => ReactNode)

components.example:
<ResourceTable
  stackAt={40}
  columns={[{ key: "name", label: "Name" }, { key: "joined", label: "Joined", date: true }]}
  rows={rows}
  status={(row) => ({ label: row.active ? "Active" : "Away", tone: row.active ? "bg-emerald-100 text-emerald-800" : "bg-zinc-100 text-zinc-600" })}
  menu
  actions={(row) => [{ id: "edit", label: "Edit", run: () => edit(row) }, { id: "delete", label: "Delete", tone: "danger", run: () => remove(row) }]}
  sorts={sorts} sortable={new Set(["name", "joined"])}
  sortHeading={(key, label) => <SortHeading sortKey={key} label={label} sorts={sorts} onSort={(k, d) => setSorts((s) => headerSort(s, k, d))} />}
  selectable selected={selected} onSelect={toggleRow} onSelectPage={(on) => setSelected(on ? new Set(rows.map((r) => r.id)) : new Set())}
  page={page} pages={pages} from={from} to={from + rows.length} total={total} pageSize={pageSize} onPage={setPage} onPageSize={setPageSize}
/>
notes: Rows need an `id` string. `columns` is `{ key, label, date? }[]`; cells show `row[key]` unless `cell` returns other text.
Fully controlled: pass `sorts`, `page`, `pages`, `from`, `to`, `total`, `pageSize` and `selected`, and update them in the callbacks. Do the sorting, filtering and slicing yourself.
`stackAt` is the container width in rem below which rows become cards (24 to 112 in steps of 8). The default is at least 80, so tables in narrow layouts stack; lower it to keep a table.
`actions(row)` returns `{ id, label, tone?, run }[]`. Add `menu` to show them behind a ⋯ button; without it they render as inline links, which suits one or two actions.
`status(row)` adds a pill column; `busy` shows `loading`; no rows shows `empty`.
`fill` makes the table fill a fixed-height parent with a sticky header.

components.name: Select
components.summary: A labelled select with a custom menu, single or multiple, with an optional clear option and error line.
components.example: <Select label="Fruit" options={[{ value: "apple", label: "Apple" }, { value: "pear", label: "Pear" }]} value={fruit} placeholder="Pick one" clearable onChange={setFruit} />
notes: Single: `value` + `onChange`. Multiple: `multiple`, `values` + `onToggle(value)`, and `summary` for the closed text (e.g. "2 selected").
`clearable` adds a first option that sets the value to "" and shows `placeholder`.
`option` renders each option and the selected value; `chevron` replaces the arrow; `labelled={false}` hides the label and error.
`preset={DropdownPreset.TOP}` opens the menu above.

components.name: Slider
components.summary: A single-value slider built on a native range input.
components.example: <Slider label="Volume" formId="audio" max={100} defaultValue={40} labelPos="r" onChange={(event) => setVolume(Number(event.currentTarget.value))} />
notes: `labelPos` is `"l"`, `"r"` (fixed-width label beside the bar) or `"i"` (inside the thumb).
`defaultValue` sets the start; it is uncontrolled after that, so read changes from the input/change events.
`labelParse` formats the label.

components.name: SmartGridView
components.summary: A masonry grid that places tiles by their aspect ratio to keep columns even, with infinite scroll.
components.example: [photo.id, [photo.height / photo.width, ]]))} onScrollEnd={loadMore} />
notes: Each tile carries a height ratio (height ÷ width) used for placement.
`columns` fixes the column count; otherwise it adapts to width.
`onScrollEnd` fires within `threshold` px of the bottom; set `loading` while fetching to show `template` placeholders.
`images` is a record of key → `[ratio, node]`.

components.name: SortHeading
components.summary: A column heading with ascending and descending arrows that shows its rank in a multi-column sort.
components.example: <th><SortHeading sortKey="name" label="Name" sorts={sorts} onSort={(key, direction) => setSorts((s) => headerSort(s, key, direction))} /></th>
notes: Pair it with `headerSort` from the `sorts` module to compute the next `sorts`.
Usually rendered through ResourceTable's `sortHeading` slot; it also works in any `<th>`.
The column key prop is `sortKey` (React reserves `key`).

components.name: TextEditor
components.summary: A markdown editor (CodeMirror) with a formatting toolbar, live styling, a character counter and insertable snippets such as `{{first_name}}`.

props.name: caption
props.type: ((text: string, labelId: string, forId: string, labelled: boolean) => ReactNode)

props.name: status
props.type: ((text: string, maxLength: number | undefined, id: string) => ReactNode)

components.example: <TextEditor label="Message" formId="email" value={body} onChange={setBody} maxLength={2000} snippets={[{ label: "First name", text: "{{first_name}}" }]} />
notes: Needs the CodeMirror and markdown-it peer dependencies.
The value is markdown text.
`snippets` (`{ label, text }[]`) fills the Insert menu; `variableClass(name)` styles `{{name}}` tokens, e.g. to flag unknown variables.
`tools` limits the toolbar groups; `rows` sets the height in lines.
Read-only is `readOnly`.

components.name: TextboxA
components.summary: A filled text field with the label below it; becomes a textarea when `height` is above 3.25.
components.example: <TextboxA label="Postcode" formId="address" mode="numeric" guard={/^\d{0,5}$/} maxLength={5} />
notes: `guard` is a RegExp the whole value must match; keystrokes that break it are rejected (e.g. `/^\d{0,5}$/`).
`mode` sets the keyboard and input type (email, tel, numeric, decimal, …).
`height` is in rem; `wrap` lets long lines wrap.

`secret` makes it a password input with a show/hide button (needs `textbox.reveal.css`); `showIcon` / `hideIcon` take text or an icon, and `revealed` is the shown state (Svelte: `bind:revealed`; React: `revealed` + `onReveal`, or leave it uncontrolled).

components.name: TextboxB
components.summary: An outlined text field whose label sits inside until focus or input, then floats onto the top border. A line under it is always reserved for the error so the layout never jumps.
components.example: <TextboxB label="Email" formId="signup" mode="email" value={email} error={emailError} onChange={(event) => setEmail(event.currentTarget.value)} />
notes: The label and border-gap use the container background (`bg-inherit`); set `className` with a `bg-*` when the field sits on a coloured surface.
No placeholder: the label plays that role. Use TextboxC if you need one.
`caption` replaces the label and `message` the error line.
`secret` adds a password show/hide button, exactly as on TextboxA.

components.name: TextboxC
components.summary: The same outlined field as TextboxB, but the label always sits on the border and a placeholder is allowed.
components.example: <TextboxC label="Address" formId="checkout" placeholder="Street, city, postcode" height={6} wrap />
notes: Shares `textbox.b.css` with TextboxB.
`secret` adds a password show/hide button, exactly as on TextboxA.

components.name: Toggle
components.summary: An on/off switch backed by a checkbox.
components.example: <Toggle label="Notifications" formId="settings" onChange={(event) => setOn(event.currentTarget.checked)} />
notes: Colour the on state with `trackClass="peer-checked:bg-indigo-600"`.
The checkbox's `value` is "true" or "false" after a change.

components.name: Tooltip
components.summary: Wraps a trigger and shows a small popup beside it on hover and keyboard focus.
components.example:
<Tooltip content="Saves a draft without publishing">
  {(trigger) => <button {...trigger} className="field-box">Save draft</button>}
</Tooltip>
notes: `content` is a string or a snippet; it renders inside `role="tooltip"`.
`preset` takes a DropdownPreset for the side (TOP by default, BOTTOM, LEFT, RIGHT).
It shows on hover (pointer devices only) and whenever focus is inside the trigger, so give non-focusable triggers `tabindex="0"`.
`interactive` keeps it open while the pointer is over it so links inside can be clicked; `open` pins it visible.
The default bubble is dark; restyle it with `innerModalClass` (e.g. `bg-white text-zinc-700 border border-zinc-200`). `--tooltip-shift` sets the slide-in distance.
`children` is the trigger. Pass a function `(trigger) => node` to receive `aria-describedby` and spread it on the trigger element.

components.name: UploadPanel
components.summary: A drop zone / file picker with an upload queue, progress bars, retry, and a Clear finished button. You provide the transport.
components.example: api.upload(file, folder, progress)} tag={() => {folder}}>
notes: `upload(file, progress)` must return a promise; call `progress(sent, total)` as bytes go out and throw to mark a failure (the error message is shown with Retry).
`isDuplicate(error)` turns a thrown error into a "Duplicate" note instead of a failure.
Children render under the drop zone, e.g. a Select for the destination folder; `tag(upload)` renders next to each file in the queue.
`concurrency` caps parallel uploads; `onSettled` fires when the queue empties.
A ref exposes `add(files)` to queue files from elsewhere (e.g. a paste handler).

helpers.summary: `DropdownPreset` (TOP, BOTTOM, LEFT, RIGHT), `DropdownAnchor`, `PanelPreset` (TOP, BOTTOM, LEFT, RIGHT), `CardPreset` and `Interact` (HOVER, CLICK, HOVER_N_CLICK). Use on client-rendered pages.
The same presets for server-rendered or statically generated pages.
`Sort`, `SortDirection` and `headerSort(sorts, key, direction, mode?)`, which returns the next sort list when a SortHeading arrow is clicked (clicking the active direction removes that sort).
`DIAL_COUNTRIES`, `DialCountry`, `joinPhone`, `splitPhone`, `digitsOnly` and `phoneIssue(stored)` (returns an error message or null) for PhoneField values.
`ify(...classes)` joins truthy class names; `Content` is the string-or-render-function prop type.
